subject: ELEC
title: Personal Finance (S1) & College/Career Readiness (S2)
description: Semester 1 is a full personal finance course aligned to the Jump$tart National Standards and California's personal finance graduation requirement (AB 2927): earning income and paychecks, budgeting, banking, credit and debt, federal and California taxes, insurance, investing and retirement, consumer protection and fraud, and renting. Semester 2 is college and career readiness for a California homeschool senior: career exploration, UC/CSU applications and Personal Insight Questions, the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application, Cal Grant and Middle Class Scholarship, community college transfer paths, resumes, job applications, work permits and interviews, and a finished homeschool transcript and private-school diploma. Because UC/CSU applications and the FAFSA/CADAA open in the fall, week 1 sets a deadline calendar so real submissions happen on time; Semester 2 then completes, verifies, and builds on them.
framework: Jump$tart National Standards for Personal Financial Education (2021) and California AB 2927 personal finance topics; California College and Career Readiness (CSAC, UC, CSU, CCC guidance)

standards.PF-EARN-1: Explain how education, skills, and career choices affect lifetime income, and compare sources of income (wages, salary, tips, self-employment, benefits).
standards.PF-EARN-2: Read a paycheck and pay stub: gross vs. net pay, payroll deductions (federal/CA withholding, FICA, CA SDI), and complete Form W-4 and the CA DE 4.
standards.PF-EARN-3: Explain federal and California income taxes and file a basic return (Form W-2, Form 1040, CA Form 540, CA Franchise Tax Board, CalEITC/Young Child Tax Credit, free filing options).
standards.PF-SPEND-1: Create, follow, and revise a spending plan (budget) that balances needs, wants, savings, and goals.
standards.PF-SPEND-2: Make informed consumer decisions: comparison shopping, opportunity cost, transportation costs, and housing choices including renting and leases.
standards.PF-SPEND-3: Recognize consumer rights and protections, and prevent and respond to fraud, scams, and identity theft (CFPB, FTC, CA DFPI, CA tenant law).
standards.PF-SAVE-1: Compare financial institutions and accounts (banks, credit unions, checking, savings, debit, digital payments, FDIC/NCUA insurance) and manage an account.
standards.PF-SAVE-2: Set savings goals, build an emergency fund, and calculate simple and compound interest and the time value of money.
standards.PF-INVEST-1: Explain the relationship between risk and return and describe stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and index funds.
standards.PF-INVEST-2: Compare retirement accounts (401(k)/403(b), traditional and Roth IRA, CalSavers, employer match) and their tax treatment.
standards.PF-INVEST-3: Apply diversification, dollar-cost averaging, and fee comparison, and recognize behavioral biases and investment fraud.
standards.PF-CREDIT-1: Explain credit reports and credit scores, how they are built and used, and how to obtain free reports and dispute errors.
standards.PF-CREDIT-2: Compare the costs of credit cards, auto loans, personal loans, and predatory products (APR, fees, minimum payments, payday loans, buy-now-pay-later).
standards.PF-CREDIT-3: Manage and repay debt, including student loans (federal vs. private, subsidized vs. unsubsidized, repayment plans) and debt-reduction strategies.
standards.PF-RISK-1: Explain how insurance manages risk (premium, deductible, copay, coinsurance, out-of-pocket maximum) and when to self-insure.
standards.PF-RISK-2: Compare auto, health (Covered California, Medi-Cal, employer plans), renters, disability, and life insurance and choose appropriate coverage.
standards.CCR-1: Assess interests, skills, and values and research careers using labor-market data to set postsecondary and career goals.
standards.CCR-2: Compare postsecondary pathways in California: UC, CSU, California Community Colleges, private/independent colleges, apprenticeships, military, and direct employment.
standards.CCR-3: Complete UC and CSU applications, including a–g course reporting, activities, and the UC Personal Insight Questions.
standards.CCR-4: Complete the FAFSA or California Dream Act Application (CADAA), including the FSA ID/StudentAid.gov account, contributors, and the Student Aid Index.
standards.CCR-5: Apply for California state aid and scholarships (Cal Grant, Middle Class Scholarship, California College Promise Grant, WebGrants) and compare financial aid offers.
standards.CCR-6: Plan community college and transfer paths (Associate Degree for Transfer, UC Transfer Admission Guarantee, ASSIST.org articulation, CTE certificates).
standards.CCR-7: Write a professional resume, cover letter, and references list tailored to a specific job or program.
standards.CCR-8: Prepare for and perform in interviews and professional communication (STAR answers, email etiquette, follow-up, workplace conduct).
standards.CCR-9: Complete job applications and employment paperwork, including the California work permit for minors, Form I-9, W-4, and workers' rights under California labor law.
standards.CCR-10: Assemble homeschool academic records: transcript, course descriptions, credit and GPA calculation, and a diploma issued by the student's private school (PSA).
standards.CCR-11: Build a transition plan: compare offers, accept admission or employment, budget the first year, and complete enrollment steps.

units.title: Earning Income, Paychecks & Budgeting
units.big_idea: Income is limited, so a written spending plan turns your paycheck into your priorities.

units.title: Banking & Payments
units.big_idea: Choosing the right accounts and payment tools keeps money safe, cheap, and accessible.

units.title: Credit & Debt
units.big_idea: Credit is a tool that costs money; your borrowing history follows you and shapes future costs.

units.title: Taxes
units.big_idea: Taxes fund public goods, and understanding forms and credits lets you keep what you are owed.

units.title: Insurance & Managing Risk
units.big_idea: Insurance transfers large financial risks you cannot afford to carry alone.

units.title: Investing, Compound Interest & Retirement
units.big_idea: Time plus compound growth, diversification, and low fees build long-term wealth.

units.title: Consumer Protection, Fraud & Renting
units.big_idea: Knowing your rights and the warning signs of scams protects your money and your home.

units.title: Postsecondary Pathways & College Applications
units.big_idea: Many California pathways lead to a good career; strong applications tell a clear, honest story.

units.title: Paying for College: FAFSA, Dream Act & State Aid
units.big_idea: Free money comes first; the FAFSA or CADAA unlocks federal, Cal Grant, and college aid.

units.title: Community College & Transfer
units.big_idea: California's community colleges are an affordable, guaranteed route to a degree, credential, or UC/CSU transfer.

units.title: Career Readiness: Resumes, Applications & Interviews
units.big_idea: Employers hire evidence: a targeted resume, accurate paperwork, and a prepared interview.

units.title: Homeschool Records, Diploma & Launch Plan
units.big_idea: A complete transcript, diploma, and first-year plan make the transition to adulthood official.

objectives: Connect education and career choices to lifetime earnings
Build a senior-year financial and application deadline calendar

days.title: Why personal finance
days.work: Take the NGPF pre-assessment and write a money autobiography (one page) on how your family talked about money and one financial goal for age 25.

days.title: Earnings and education
days.work: Use BLS median-earnings-by-education data to graph weekly earnings and unemployment rates for six education levels, then write three conclusions.

days.title: Career salary research
days.work: Pick three careers on CaliforniaColleges.edu and record typical California salary, required training, and projected growth for each.

days.title: Senior deadline calendar
days.work: Mark real dates on a calendar: FAFSA/CADAA opens Oct 1, Cal State Apply and UC application windows (UC due Nov 30), and the March Cal Grant deadline; set reminders to submit applications this fall.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 10-question quiz on income types and the education-earnings link and present your calendar to a parent.

weeks.assessment: Quiz on income concepts plus a completed senior deadline calendar.

objectives: Calculate gross and net pay
Complete a W-4 and CA DE 4 correctly

days.title: Gross vs. net
days.work: Calculate gross pay for hourly jobs at California minimum wage with overtime (over 8 hours/day or 40/week) for three sample schedules.

days.title: Reading a pay stub
days.work: Label every line on an NGPF sample pay stub (federal and state withholding, Social Security, Medicare, CA SDI, YTD) and find net pay.

days.title: Form W-4
days.work: Fill out a practice IRS Form W-4 for a single teen with one job and explain each step in writing.

days.title: Form DE 4 and benefits
days.work: Complete a practice CA DE 4 and compare two job offers that include health insurance and 401(k) match to see total compensation.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Play NGPF 'Paycheck' scenarios and solve five net-pay problems on a short quiz.

weeks.assessment: Net-pay quiz and accuracy check of practice W-4/DE 4.

objectives: Distinguish needs, wants, and savings
Create a balanced monthly budget

days.title: Needs vs. wants
days.work: Sort 30 expense cards into needs and wants, then defend five borderline items (phone plan, car, streaming) in writing.

days.title: Track your spending
days.work: Begin a 7-day expense tracker logging every purchase, and watch the Khan Academy budgeting video, taking notes on the 50/30/20 rule.

days.title: Budget spreadsheet
days.work: Build a monthly budget spreadsheet with formulas for income, fixed and variable expenses, savings, and the balance for a $2,400 net income.

days.title: Budget challenge
days.work: Play the NGPF budget simulation (e.g., 'Budget Challenge' or SPENT) and record three decisions you would change.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise your budget after a surprise $400 car repair and write a paragraph on how you balanced it.

weeks.assessment: Graded budget spreadsheet with a balanced revision.

objectives: Use comparison shopping and opportunity cost
Calculate the total cost of owning a car

days.title: Opportunity cost
days.work: Analyze three of your own recent purchases for opportunity cost and compute what each would be worth saved at 5% for 10 years.

days.title: Comparison shopping
days.work: Compare unit prices for 10 grocery items across two stores or websites and calculate monthly savings.

days.title: Marketing tactics
days.work: Identify five persuasive techniques in online ads (scarcity, social proof, anchoring, free trials, influencer posts) using real examples.

days.title: Cost of a car
days.work: Calculate the 5-year total cost of ownership for a used vs. new car including California registration, insurance, gas, and maintenance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 1 test: paychecks, budgeting, and consumer choice scenarios, plus final 7-day spending reflection.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test and car-cost comparison project.

objectives: Compare financial institutions and account features
Explain FDIC and NCUA insurance
materials: FDIC Money Smart for Young Adults
account fee schedules from two local institutions

days.title: Why bank
days.work: Complete the FDIC Money Smart module on bank accounts and list the costs of being unbanked (check-cashing and money-order fees).

days.title: Compare institutions
days.work: Compare fee schedules of a local bank and a credit union: minimum balance, monthly fees, overdraft fees, ATM network.

days.title: Account management
days.work: Practice a month of transactions in a sample check register, including a debit card purchase, direct deposit, and a pending charge.

days.title: Reconcile
days.work: Reconcile the register with a sample monthly statement and find two errors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a recommendation memo choosing an account for your first job and take a short banking quiz.

weeks.assessment: Banking quiz and account recommendation memo.

objectives: Calculate simple and compound interest on savings
Use digital payments safely

days.title: Emergency fund
days.work: Calculate a 3-month emergency fund from your Unit 1 budget and plan how many months to reach it.

days.title: Simple vs. compound
days.work: Compute simple and compound interest by hand for $1,000 at 4% over 5 years, then verify in a spreadsheet with =FV.

days.title: Rule of 72
days.work: Use the Rule of 72 to estimate doubling times at 2%, 6%, and 10% and compare to spreadsheet results.

days.title: Digital payments
days.work: Compare Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, and debit cards for fees, fraud protection, and FDIC coverage; write five safe-use rules.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a savings-goal plan with interest projection and a 10-question quiz.

weeks.assessment: Savings plan with compound-interest projection and quiz.

objectives: Explain what goes into a credit score
Read a credit report and dispute an error

days.title: What is credit
days.work: Watch the Khan Academy credit score video and diagram the five FICO factors with their approximate weights.

days.title: Reading a report
days.work: Annotate a sample credit report: personal info, accounts, payment history, inquiries, and collections.

days.title: Who checks your credit
days.work: Research how landlords, employers, insurers, and lenders use credit and write a one-paragraph summary for each.

days.title: Disputes
days.work: Find two errors in a sample report and draft a dispute letter following CFPB guidance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Rank six credit profiles from best to worst score and justify your order; short quiz.

weeks.assessment: Credit profile ranking and dispute letter.

weeks.topic: Credit cards, loans & the cost of borrowing
objectives: Calculate the cost of carrying a balance
Compare credit products and identify predatory lending

days.title: Card terms
days.work: Compare the Schumer boxes of three real credit card offers (student, secured, rewards) for APR, fees, and penalties.

days.title: Minimum payment trap
days.work: Calculate how long a $2,000 balance at 24% APR takes to repay with minimum payments vs. $150/month.

days.title: Auto and personal loans
days.work: Use an amortization spreadsheet to compare a 36- vs. 72-month auto loan for total interest paid.

days.title: Predatory products
days.work: Research payday loans, rent-to-own, and buy-now-pay-later; compute the APR of a $15-per-$100 two-week payday loan.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 'first credit card' plan (which card, limits, autopay) and take a borrowing-costs quiz.

weeks.assessment: Borrowing-cost calculations and first credit card plan.

objectives: Compare federal and private student loans
Apply debt snowball and avalanche strategies

days.title: Student loan basics
days.work: Read the StudentAid.gov loan types page and make a comparison chart of Direct Subsidized, Unsubsidized, PLUS, and private loans.

days.title: Loan Simulator
days.work: Use the StudentAid.gov Loan Simulator to estimate monthly payments on $27,000 under standard and income-driven plans.

days.title: Debt strategies
days.work: Pay down a sample four-debt portfolio using both avalanche and snowball methods in a spreadsheet and compare interest paid.

days.title: When debt goes wrong
days.work: Research collections, default, and wage garnishment, and list three resources (nonprofit credit counseling, CFPB) for help.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 3 test on credit reports, credit costs, and debt management.

weeks.assessment: Unit 3 test and debt-repayment spreadsheet.

objectives: Explain progressive income tax brackets
Identify federal, state, and local taxes Californians pay

days.title: Why taxes
days.work: List public goods funded by federal and California taxes and compare the share of revenue from income, payroll, and sales taxes.

days.title: Brackets
days.work: Calculate federal income tax for three incomes using the current bracket table and find each marginal and effective rate.

days.title: California taxes
days.work: Use the CA FTB rate schedule to compute state income tax for the same incomes and add local sales tax on a $1,000 purchase in your county.

days.title: Tax myths
days.work: Debunk 'a raise can put me in a higher bracket and lower my take-home pay' with a worked example.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Solve a five-problem tax-calculation quiz.

weeks.assessment: Tax-calculation quiz.

objectives: Complete a basic Form 1040 and CA 540 from a W-2
Identify credits and free filing options
materials: IRS Form 1040 and CA Form 540 (practice copies)
IRS Understanding Taxes / NGPF tax simulation

days.title: Reading a W-2
days.work: Label each box on a sample W-2 and match boxes to the lines where they go on the 1040 and 540.

days.title: Form 1040
days.work: Complete a practice Form 1040 for a single filer with one W-2 and the standard deduction; compute the refund or amount owed.

days.title: CA Form 540
days.work: Complete a practice CA Form 540 using the same W-2 and check eligibility for the California Earned Income Tax Credit.

days.title: Filing options
days.work: Compare IRS Free File, VITA sites, and the FTB's CalFile, and list documents to keep and how long to keep them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 4 assessment: file a complete practice federal and California return from a new W-2.

weeks.assessment: Accuracy of practice 1040 and 540 returns.

objectives: Explain premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket maximums
Compare health coverage options in California

days.title: How insurance works
days.work: Play an NGPF risk-pooling simulation and explain in writing why insurers can pay large claims.

days.title: Insurance math
days.work: Calculate what you pay for three medical scenarios under a high-deductible vs. low-deductible plan.

days.title: Health coverage options
days.work: Compare staying on a parent's plan to age 26, student health plans, employer plans, Covered California, and Medi-Cal.

days.title: Choosing a plan
days.work: Use Covered California's shop-and-compare tool for a sample 19-year-old and choose a plan with a written justification.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on insurance vocabulary and a health-plan cost comparison problem.

weeks.assessment: Insurance quiz and plan-choice justification.

objectives: Compare auto coverage types and California minimums
Decide which insurance a young adult needs
materials: CA Department of Insurance consumer pages

days.title: Auto insurance
days.work: Explain liability, collision, comprehensive, and uninsured motorist coverage and look up California's minimum liability limits.

days.title: Auto quote lab
days.work: Get two practice online quotes (no purchase) changing deductible and car type, and record how premiums change.

days.title: Renters insurance
days.work: Inventory and value your belongings and price a renters policy; calculate cost per day of coverage.

days.title: Disability and life
days.work: Compare term vs. whole life and explain when a young adult would need disability or life insurance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Build a personal insurance plan for age 22 listing coverages, estimated premiums, and deductibles; unit test.

weeks.assessment: Unit 5 test and personal insurance plan.

objectives: Model compound growth over decades
Explain risk and return of stocks, bonds, and funds

days.title: Time is money
days.work: Model two savers in a spreadsheet: one invests $200/month from 22–32, the other from 32–65, at 7%; graph the results.

days.title: What is a stock
days.work: Watch the Khan Academy stocks video and explain ownership, dividends, and capital gains with an example company.

days.title: Bonds and cash
days.work: Compare Treasury bonds, I bonds, CDs, and corporate bonds for risk and return.

days.title: Funds
days.work: Compare an S&P 500 index fund and an actively managed fund using their expense ratios and 10-year returns.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on asset classes and compound-growth calculations.

weeks.assessment: Compound growth spreadsheet and asset-class quiz.

objectives: Build a diversified portfolio
Calculate the long-term cost of fees and spot investment scams

days.title: Diversification
days.work: Simulate a single-stock vs. index portfolio through a market crash using historical returns and compare losses.

days.title: Fees matter
days.work: Calculate the 40-year difference in a $100,000 balance invested at 0.05% vs. 1% annual fees.

days.title: Behavioral biases
days.work: Read about loss aversion, herd behavior, and FOMO and connect each to a real event (2008 crash, meme stocks, crypto collapse).

days.title: Investment fraud
days.work: Use FINRA BrokerCheck and the SEC's Investor.gov warning signs to evaluate three sample 'opportunities'.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create an asset allocation for ages 20, 40, and 60 with a paragraph explaining each.

weeks.assessment: Asset allocation project and fraud evaluation.

objectives: Compare 401(k), traditional IRA, Roth IRA, and CalSavers
Calculate the value of an employer match

days.title: Why retirement now
days.work: Watch the Khan Academy 401(k) and IRA videos and chart tax treatment of traditional vs. Roth accounts.

days.title: Employer match
days.work: Calculate the free money from a 50% match up to 6% on a $50,000 salary over 10 years with growth.

days.title: Roth for teens
days.work: Explain how a teen with earned income can open a custodial Roth IRA and project a $1,000 contribution to age 65.

days.title: CalSavers and Social Security
days.work: Research California's CalSavers program and read your projected Social Security benefits at ssa.gov examples.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 6 test on investing and retirement accounts.

weeks.assessment: Unit 6 test.

objectives: Recognize common scams targeting young adults
Respond to fraud and identity theft

days.title: Scam spotting
days.work: Analyze 10 real phishing texts, emails, and job-offer scams and label the red flags in each.

days.title: Identity theft
days.work: Complete the FDIC Money Smart identity-theft lesson and walk through the IdentityTheft.gov recovery plan steps.

days.title: Credit freezes
days.work: Explain how to place free credit freezes at Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion and why it matters before age 18.

days.title: Your rights
days.work: Research consumer rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and California law, and draft a CFPB or DFPI complaint for a sample problem.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a one-page scam-prevention guide for a younger sibling or grandparent; short quiz.

weeks.assessment: Scam-prevention guide and quiz.

weeks.topic: Renting your first apartment & semester capstone
objectives: Read a lease and estimate move-in costs
Integrate all personal finance skills in a life-budget capstone

days.title: Rental search
days.work: Find three rentals near a chosen college or job, apply the 30% rule, and calculate total move-in costs.

days.title: Reading a lease
days.work: Annotate a sample California lease for rent, deposit, late fees, repairs, and termination; list your tenant rights and the legal security deposit return timeline.

days.title: Roommates
days.work: Write a roommate agreement covering rent split, utilities, guests, and chores.

days.title: Capstone budget
days.work: Build a complete first-year independent life budget combining a job's net pay, rent, insurance, transportation, savings, and debt payments.

days.title: Semester final
days.work: Take the NGPF post-assessment/semester final and present your capstone budget to a parent.

weeks.assessment: Semester final exam and life-budget capstone.

objectives: Identify interests, strengths, and values
Research careers with labor-market data

days.title: Interest inventory
days.work: Take the career interest assessment on CaliforniaColleges.edu and the O*NET Interest Profiler, then compare results.

days.title: Strengths and values
days.work: Complete a work-values ranking and list five strengths with evidence from homeschool projects, jobs, or activities.

days.title: Career research
days.work: Research three careers in the Occupational Outlook Handbook: duties, education, pay, outlook, and California openings.

days.title: Informational interview
days.work: Prepare 10 questions and conduct a 20-minute informational interview with a professional in one target career.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a two-page career exploration report with a five-year goal.

weeks.assessment: Career exploration report.

objectives: Compare UC, CSU, CCC, private, apprenticeship, and military paths
Build a balanced college list

days.title: Systems compared
days.work: Make a chart comparing the UC, CSU, California Community Colleges, and private colleges by mission, cost, size, and admission requirements.

days.title: Beyond college
days.work: Research a California registered apprenticeship, a CTE certificate, and military enlistment requirements.

days.title: College search
days.work: Use CaliforniaColleges.edu and College Scorecard to find eight schools and record graduation rate, median debt, and earnings.

days.title: Net price
days.work: Run three college net price calculators with your family and compare estimated costs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Submit a balanced list of likely, match, and reach options with a pathway rationale.

weeks.assessment: Balanced college/pathway list with data.

objectives: Explain how UC and CSU evaluate homeschool applicants
Draft course descriptions for the transcript
materials: UC and CSU homeschool admissions pages
list of completed courses and grades

days.title: UC and homeschoolers
days.work: Read the UC admissions page for homeschooled students and summarize how a–g can be met (AP exams, college courses, a–g approved online courses, admission by examination).

days.title: CSU and homeschoolers
days.work: Read CSU's homeschool guidance and list required documents and how to report courses in Cal State Apply.

days.work: Build a four-year course list from your homeschool records with a–g letter, grade, and semester credits for each course.

days.work: Write course descriptions (texts, labs, assessments) for three courses that will appear in the counselor packet.

objectives: Complete UC and Cal State Apply application sections
Report courses, activities, and awards accurately

days.work: Enter or practice entering your self-reported academic record exactly from your transcript.

objectives: Choose four UC PIQs that showcase different strengths

days.work: Chart Cal Grant A, B, and C: what each pays, at which schools, and eligibility requirements.

days.work: Read the MCS page and estimate what a sample UC or CSU student might receive.

days.title: Community college aid
days.work: Research the California College Promise Grant and local free-tuition programs at a nearby community college.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Build a total state-aid estimate for your top three schools.

weeks.assessment: State-aid estimate for three schools.

objectives: Find legitimate scholarships
Write a reusable scholarship essay

days.title: Finding scholarships
days.work: Search local, community, employer, and online scholarships and list 10 with deadlines and requirements.

days.title: Scam spotting
days.work: Use FTC guidance to identify red flags of scholarship scams (fees, guaranteed winnings).

days.title: Essay draft
days.work: Draft a 500-word scholarship essay that can be adapted to multiple prompts.

days.title: Applications
days.work: Complete and submit (or fully prepare) two scholarship applications.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise the essay with parent feedback and log applications in a tracker.

weeks.assessment: Two completed scholarship applications.

objectives: Calculate net cost from aid offers
Make a financially sound college decision

days.title: Decoding offers
days.work: Label grants, loans, and work-study on three sample aid offers that use different formats.

days.title: Net cost spreadsheet
days.work: Build a spreadsheet comparing four-year net cost and expected loan debt across offers.

days.title: Debt-to-income
days.work: Compare projected loan payments to starting salaries for your intended major using College Scorecard data.

days.title: Appeals
days.work: Write a professional financial-aid appeal letter for a sample changed circumstance.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 9 test and a written decision memo choosing a school based on fit and cost.

weeks.assessment: Unit 9 test and decision memo.

objectives: Explain community college programs and costs
Complete the CCCApply steps
materials: local community college website and catalog

days.title: CCC programs
days.work: Explore a local college catalog and list three certificates, three AA/AS degrees, and their unit requirements.

days.title: CCCApply
days.work: Walk through CCCApply and record residency, education, and enrollment information requirements.

days.title: Enrollment steps
days.work: Map orientation, placement (AB 705 guided self-placement), counseling, and the education plan.

days.title: Dual enrollment
days.work: Research how homeschool students take community college classes now (special admit) and what transfers.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a semester-by-semester community college plan for one goal.

weeks.assessment: Community college education plan.

objectives: Use ASSIST.org to find articulated courses
Compare ADT and TAG transfer guarantees

days.title: Transfer basics
days.work: Explain Associate Degree for Transfer (CSU guarantee) and UC Transfer Admission Guarantee eligibility.

days.title: ASSIST lab
days.work: Use ASSIST.org to find which courses at a local community college meet major prep for your target UC/CSU major.

days.title: General education
days.work: Map the Cal-GETC general education pattern into a two-year schedule.

days.title: Transfer plan
days.work: Build a full 60-unit two-year transfer plan with TAG/ADT deadlines.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present your transfer plan and compare four-year net cost with the direct freshman path.

weeks.assessment: Two-year transfer plan and cost comparison.

objectives: Write a targeted one-page resume
Write a tailored cover letter

days.title: Resume formats
days.work: Compare chronological, skills-based, and student resume samples and pick a format.

days.title: Accomplishments
days.work: Rewrite 10 duties into quantified accomplishment statements using strong action verbs.

days.title: Full resume
days.work: Draft a one-page resume including homeschool education, volunteer work, skills, and certifications.

days.title: Cover letter
days.work: Write a tailored cover letter for a real local job posting, matching keywords from the posting.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise resume and cover letter after a parent or mentor review and request two references.

weeks.assessment: Final resume and cover letter scored with a rubric.

objectives: Complete online job applications accurately
Obtain a California work permit if under 18
vocabulary: Statement of Intent to Employ a Minor
materials: CA form B1-1 (Statement of Intent to Employ a Minor and Request for Work Permit)

days.title: Job search
days.work: Find five local jobs on employer sites and job boards and evaluate pay, schedule, and requirements.

days.title: Online application
days.work: Complete a full online job application, including availability, work history, and screening questions.

days.title: Work permits
days.work: Read California's minor work permit rules and complete form B1-1; learn where a private-school student obtains the permit (typically the local district) and teen hour limits.

days.title: Hiring paperwork
days.work: Practice Form I-9 identity documents, a W-4, and direct-deposit forms.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Submit one real application (or a complete practice packet) and log it in a job tracker.

weeks.assessment: Completed application packet and work permit form.

objectives: Answer common interview questions with STAR stories
Perform a mock interview professionally

days.title: Interview types
days.work: Compare phone, video, group, and behavioral interviews and research the company for a target job.

days.title: STAR stories
days.work: Write five STAR stories from your experience (teamwork, conflict, failure, leadership, initiative).

days.title: Elevator pitch
days.work: Write and record a 30-second elevator pitch, then revise after watching it back.

days.title: Mock interview
days.work: Complete a 20-minute recorded mock interview with an adult using 10 common questions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-score the recording with a rubric and send a professional thank-you email.

weeks.assessment: Mock interview rubric score and thank-you email.

objectives: Explain California workers' rights
Practice professional communication

days.title: Professional communication
days.work: Write three professional emails: requesting time off, following up on an application, and asking a supervisor for feedback.

days.title: Workers' rights
days.work: Research California minimum wage, overtime, meal and rest breaks, and paid sick leave and make a rights card.

days.title: Workplace safety and harassment
days.work: Learn how to report unsafe conditions and harassment and the role of Cal/OSHA and the Labor Commissioner.

days.title: Job offer
days.work: Evaluate two sample job offers by total compensation, schedule, growth, and commute cost.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 11 test on career readiness and employment law.

weeks.assessment: Unit 11 test.

objectives: Finalize an official homeschool transcript
Understand the private-school diploma and graduation records
materials: copy of filed Private School Affidavit

days.title: GPA and credits
days.work: Calculate cumulative unweighted GPA and total credits (10 credits per year-long course) from your four-year record.

days.title: Final transcript
days.work: Finalize the transcript with school name, CDS/affidavit info, courses by year, a–g letters, grades, GPA, and graduation date, signed by the administrator.

days.title: Diploma and graduation
days.work: Learn that the private school (PSA) administrator issues the diploma, review graduation requirements, and compare with the CHSPE as an alternative.

days.title: Records packet
days.work: Assemble a permanent records packet: transcript, course descriptions, reading lists, test scores, work samples, and copies of affidavits.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Parent signs and seals the final transcript; student creates digital and paper copies.

weeks.assessment: Signed final transcript and records packet.

objectives: Create a first-year transition plan
Present a personal finance and career portfolio

days.title: Final decisions
days.work: Complete enrollment or job acceptance steps (Statement of Intent to Register, housing, orientation) or a gap-year plan with milestones.

days.title: First-year budget
days.work: Update the Unit 7 life budget with actual aid, wages, and costs for your first year after graduation.

days.title: Adulting checklist
days.work: Complete a checklist: voter registration, Selective Service if applicable, health insurance, bank accounts, credit freeze, and important documents.

days.title: Portfolio
days.work: Assemble a digital portfolio with resume, transcript, PIQs, budget, and career report.

days.title: Final presentation
days.work: Present your launch plan and portfolio to family and a guest; take the course final reflection.

weeks.assessment: Capstone presentation and portfolio.
